records.text: Candace Owens says members of Victor Marx's family claimed his stories about his stepfather were untrue, including the story that he was forced to kill someone.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: We have also been contacted, I should say, by family members of Victor Marx himself who claim that his entire backstory of stuff he is saying about his stepfather simply is not true. ... He was not forced to kill anybody, that there are no bodies in the backyards of their farms, and that his stepfather Gleis Dean Kennedy was indeed a crazy man, but he did not abuse those kids.

verification.notes: The transcript contains the host report, but the family members are unnamed and no independently attributable statements were located. The existence and scope of the claimed private contacts therefore cannot be verified.

records.text: Victor Marx says that when he was about three and a half, his stepfather threatened him and forced him to cut the head off a dead cat, then placed the carcass on his head.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: I remember sitting on the ground with my arms still tied to the bedpost and then he brought an animal in, a dead cat, and he had a knife and he said, I want you to cut the head off this cat. ... And I was terrified and he said, if you don't, I'll cut your head off. So, ... yeah, about three and a half, I used the knife, cut the cat's head off, and then he put the carcass on my head and blood dripped down on me.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms this is a quoted autobiographical account. Current reporting repeats the account but provides no independent witness or record corroborating the childhood event, and Marx has publicly disputed a related characterization about wearing a severed cat head.

records.text: Victor Marx says his stepfather forced his finger onto a pistol trigger so that Marx shot and killed a man, after which the stepfather buried the victim and threatened to frame Marx.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: My stepfather, he put one hand on my wrist, and he put his finger over my trigger finger. ... And then he pushed and I pulled and I shot the guy in the head and it killed him and he shoved him in the hole and he buried him. ... He wrapped the pistol with a handkerchief and he said, if you ever tell anybody what I've done, he said, I know where this body is. ... And he said, I'll tell the police. It's your fingerprints on this pistol. And he says, they'll arrest you.

verification.notes: Transcript context confirms the autobiographical allegation. Current reporting and a named researcher found no local sheriff record of the reported homicide or later report, but absence of a record does not directly prove that the alleged childhood killing did not occur.

records.text: Victor Marx says he called the sheriff's department years later about the alleged childhood shooting, but the resulting cold case produced no findings.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: So no, I did not walk into a police station. I called the sheriff's department. and made the claim many years later. ... The reason why it is a cold case, it was 40 years old, we don't know where the house is, we don't know where he was buried, we don't know who the victim was, and my grandfather, it was my stepfather at the time, he was put in prison for unrelated charges to murder, but it was sadly drug use and bringing it in. ... there's a cold case. They could not find anything. At least I went to them to clear my conscience because I suffered for years thinking that I'd killed a person.

verification.notes: Current reporting quotes the Simpson County Sheriff office as having no record of Marx or Vaughn Victor Kennedy reporting the alleged homicide, and no record of the incident. That directly contradicts the claimed sheriff report and resulting cold case.
